# Executive summary (one page)

**What it is.** One agent design, built as 21 layers, run for eight fictional organisations: an airport, a grocer, a lender, an insurer, a hospital, a bank, an IT service desk and a carrier. The same shared code does the risky parts (permissions, approvals, safe retries, undo, privacy, audit); each organisation adds only its records and rules.

**What the tests show (synthetic, offline).** 272 of 280 scenarios pass every check with all layers on, versus 48 with them off. With all layers on there were 0 unauthorized writes, cross-customer reads, data exfiltrations, PII leaks or protected-field exposures. Switching off any single safety layer brings its failure back, which shows what each one is for.

**Cost.** Rule code, templates, small context and model routing cut simulated model cost per request by 88-94% across domains at the same pass rate (assumed token prices, 2026-11-09).

**Business case (illustrative).** With stated assumptions for each fictional organisation, base-case payback ranges from 0.3 to 1.8 months. These are planning estimates, not client results; the inputs are listed and easy to replace.

**Risks that remain.** The model is a deterministic stand-in; real model behaviour must be measured on real traffic. One known miss stays visible in every domain (a corrected reference is read wrongly). Nothing is deployed; cloud templates are written, validated and switched off.

**Decision asked.** Pick one domain, replace the assumptions with real volumes and costs, connect a real model behind the existing flag, and run the same evaluation gate on a shadow copy of real traffic before any customer sees it.
